chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Russell Smith's wife puts him out and the veterans' lawsuit
summary: After he sent money home for years, his wife evicted him; veterans' lawyers won him half the house, a car and a condominium, and he married her daughter.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: There is one story that perhaps we should tell 'cause you and I both know about it, and this is your history, but I think certainly this great man that you and I worked with and respect so highly we should mention. Since he couldn't read, we used to write his letters for him and he sent his money periodically to this lady he was married to and he didn't get home for years --
That's right.
-- and when he finally retired, he went home and she put him out.
Yeah, I know. I remember that.
She put him out.
She did, she put him out after he sent that money all those years. That's right.

All those years. When he went to California his wife -- Russell Smith, his wife -- put him out. But the most beautiful part about the story is to be told, which is so rewarding. He was a veteran of the -- he was a veteran and he went to the veterans association and explained it to them and they took her to court and they made her sell the house and give him half of the money for the house. They also took her to court and the government lawyers defended him and made her give him the automobile because he was a musician and he needed it.
True.

They made her give him the furnishings in the house that a musician needed, like the hi-fi and the record player. And they took the money -- not only did they do that, but they took the money that they got for him and bought him a condominium with about five or six apartments in it --
Oh, yes.
: -- and gave him a place to stay and let him live off the income so that he'd live to his old age in comfort, because he had been a veteran which I think is kind of rewarding --
It is.
: -- that we can know that somebody has been taken care of.
But the reward is, too, you know, he wound up marrying her daughter.
: Right. That's what I heard.
That's right, he married her daughter.
: Right.
That's right.
: That's amazing. That was --
And they stayed together clear till he died.
: That's right.
That's right.
: Quite a story there --
Yeah.
: -- which we were all involved in.
Oh, definitely. Oh, there's so many stories involved in that.
